title: Campaign 2 — validated fine-tune (corrects C1's from-init error)
objective: Does Riley Corpus v1.0 outperform the naive corpus when BOTH models fine-tune from the validated pretrained htdemucs checkpoint? Corpus is the only variable.

arms.note: SAME frozen datasets + same equal-N cap as Campaign 1 (ds_A/ds_B unchanged).

pretrained_init.transfer_coverage: 100.0% of params (529/533 keys); only the 4-key 2-stem output head reinitializes
pretrained_init.verified: CPU dry-run confirmed weights loaded (transformer norm 26->103) + trains + ckpt saves

required_config_change.why: C1's b1 config (bottom_channels 0) is NON-STANDARD htdemucs -> only 35% of stock weights fit; it could NEVER have loaded stock htdemucs (this is WHY C1 was unavoidably from-init). bottom_channels 512 = standard htdemucs -> 100% backbone transfer. Applied IDENTICALLY to both arms.

evaluation: IDENTICAL to C1 (SI-SDR/SDR + downstream note-F1 + blind), same held-out eval sets -> directly comparable
promotion_gate: unchanged/matured (benchmark + blind + cross-regime + no regressions + reproducibility + provenance)
comparability_note: C1 (from-init, non-standard 27M) vs C2 (fine-tune, standard 42M htdemucs). The DATA A/B within C2 is clean (both arms identical). C1<->C2 isolates the effect of pretrained init.
